$schema: Discovery registry implementation — per-invocation discovery files for docwriter leaf agents, consumed by gap-hunter
description: Adds a .docwriter/discoveries/ directory where 5 leaf agents write per-invocation discovery files. Gap-hunter consumes all files in a new Step 7. Bootstrap manages directory lifecycle. ROUTING-ARCHITECTURE.md and changelog updated.
assumptions: Bootstrap script has both fresh and --clean modes
ROUTING-ARCHITECTURE.md has per-pass data flow sections
Content-writer has dead gaps/notes fields in writer-output.json (will be removed)

designDecisions.decision: Directory of per-invocation files instead of single registry JSON
designDecisions.rationale: Avoids read-merge-write pattern. Each agent creates exactly one file per invocation — no locking, no corruption, naturally append-only across cycles.
Discoveries are cycle-specific artifacts, not persistent meta-knowledge. They're consumed by gap-hunter within the same run. Meta-knowledge (meta/) captures the long-term signal.
Centralizes consumption. No other agent needs to read discoveries — they either produce them or ignore them. Gap-hunter's adversarial audit role makes it the natural consumer.

designDecisions.decision: Content-writer gaps/notes fields removed from schema
designDecisions.rationale: Discovery file replaces the dead channel. Execution-coordinator only reads attempt count from writer-output.json, not gaps/notes. No reason to keep fields nobody reads.

designDecisions.decision: Step 7 (not modification of existing steps) for gap-hunter
designDecisions.rationale: Keeps existing gap-hunting logic untouched. Step 7 runs after Steps 1-6 to deduplicate before converting discoveries to gaps.
